title: Release security snapshot & approval worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is a compact, actionable snapshot for release engineers, SREs, and the security review team to validate RBAC v2 changes, audit log schema conformance, evidence automation outputs, and SIEM export readiness ahead of go-live. Use this for mid-size launches (regional model rollouts, Dedicated pool updates) where a fast but thorough signoff is required.

How to use this file:
- Owner (security) fills the RBAC and audit verification sections.
- Release lead confirms deployment details and attaches run artifacts.
- If any ‘blocker’ item is flagged, DO NOT proceed to automate rollover; follow the exception approval flow (section: Exception approvals).

Summary snapshot:
- Release: scoped model catalog update (model v1.14 -> v1.15) + serving runtime kernel swap
- Env: prod-us-east-1 (canary -> 10% -> 100%)
- Risk tier: Medium (impact to inference availability and potential telemetry schema changes)
- RBAC delta: 3 new roles introduced (inference-caller-lite, inspector-readonly, cache-ops), 2 group mappings changed (platform-ops -> dedicated-admins), 1 temporary emergency grant planned (48h)

Checklist (quick pass):
1) RBAC v2 verification:
   - Is the RBAC change set recorded in the RBAC-v2 design confluence page? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Are new roles scoped to the minimum privileges? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Has automated policy lint been run against the new role definitions (policylint job id)? -> __
   - Are group mappings and SSO sync windows documented and scheduled? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Emergency grant plan present (timeboxed, auditable)? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Audit hooks instrumented for all role-assignment events? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Notes (owner): __

2) Audit log schema conformance (quick checks):
   - Schema version targeted: audit-schema-v3 (expected fields list below)
   - Required fields present in sample payloads: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_roles, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, source_ip, user_agent, trace_id
   - Ensure field types: timestamp=RFC3339 string, event_id=uuid string, actor_roles=array[string], outcome=enum(success|failure|denied)
   - Has the schema evolution migration been applied to the logging pipeline? (log-shipper config hash) -> __
   - Do sample logs from the canary show correct mappings? (attach example file) -> __
   - Are PII redaction rules applied in pre-export stage? [YES/NO] -> __

3) SIEM export readiness:
   - Export format: newline-delimited JSON to internal-forwarder (syslog disabled for this release)
   - Field mapping verified with SOC (mapping ticket id): -> __
   - Compression/batching policy acceptable for expected token throughput? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Forwarder backpressure behavior documented (SRE contact): -> __
   - Test-forward run id and results: -> __

4) Evidence automation & artifacts:
   - Evidence automation job (evidence-collector v2) run against canary? [YES/NO] -> __
   - Evidence outputs required: RBAC diff, policy lint report, sample audit logs (24h), SIEM mapping snapshot, pipeline health metrics, signing-hash of artifacts -> __
   - Evidence storage location (GDrive / S3) -> __
   - Artifact TTL and retention policy applied (30 days for release artifacts) -> __
   - Hash and signature recorded (sha256): __

5) Risk & mitigations (short):
   - Identified risk: mis-scoped role allows read of model evals -> mitigation: temporary rate limits + audit alert on model_eval.read events
   - Identified risk: schema drift causes SIEM parsing failures -> mitigation: fallback exporter to raw-ndjson bucket + alert to SOC

Approval matrix (recommended):
- Low risk (minor docs, telemetry flags) -> release lead signoff alone
- Medium risk (this release) -> required: Security lead + Release lead + SRE owner
- High risk (any secret-handling changes, cross-tenant exposure) -> required: Security lead + CTO or Head of Platform

Exception approval flow (if any blocker present):
- Submit a compact exception package to security-exceptions@redwood.ai with: RBAC diff, justification, compensating controls, and planned rollback.
- Security lead triages within 4 business hours.
- If conditionally approved, security issues a timeboxed exception token (48h max) and requires full postmortem within 72h of expiry.

Minimum acceptance criteria to sign off (all must be YES or have approved exceptions):
- RBAC minimal scoping verified
- Audit schema validated on canary logs
- SIEM export mapping verified by SOC with at least one successful forward test
- Evidence artifacts produced and uploaded to the release evidence folder
- No open critical security findings (CVSS >= 9) against infra components in release window

Signoff block (populate names and dates):
- Release lead: _______________________   Date: _______
- SRE owner: __________________________  Date: _______
- Security lead: _______________________  Date: _______
- Exception token id (if used): ___________________

Quick runbook (commands and checks for on-call use):
1) RBAC diff and lint:
   - run: ./tools/rbac-diff --from=prod --to=staging --output=diff.json
   - run: ./tools/policylint --file=diff.json --format=summary
2) Sample log pull (canary):
   - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/canary/audit/2025-03-11/ sample-logs.jsonl
   - jq -r '.[0] | {timestamp, event_id, actor_id, action, outcome}' sample-logs.jsonl | head
3) Evidence collector:
   - ./go run ./cmd/evidence-collector --release=2025-03-12-canary --out=gs://release-evidence/2025-03-12/
4) SIEM forwarder smoke test:
   - POST sample event to forwarder endpoint and verify SOC ack (ticket): curl -X POST $FORWARDER_URL -d @sample-event.json

Notes and context (freeform):
- This compact worksheet is intentionally brief to fit into release playbooks and shiproom readouts. It is not a replacement for the full SEC pre-launch package, which should be attached when there are cross-region or high-risk changes.
- For RBAC v2 design rationale and historical changelog, see: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC-v2-design
- If you need a machine-readable checklist (CI gate), the checklist items above map 1:1 to the CI gate tokens in infra/ci/security-gates.yaml

Post-release follow-ups (automated tasks):
- Evidence-collector scheduled to re-run 24 hours after 100% rollout to capture steady-state logs
- Security will run a retrospective within 72 hours if any exception token was consumed
- SOC to confirm SIEM parser stats and provide a short report (parse success rate, dropped events) within 48 hours

Appendix A — Minimal audit event example (canonical):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-03-12T14:23:11Z",
  "event_id": "111e2222-e33b-44c4-8888-1234567890ab",
  "actor_id": "user:alice@redwood.ai",
  "actor_roles": ["platform-ops"],
  "action": "role.assign",
  "resource_type": "group",
  "resource_id": "dedicated-admins",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-98765",
  "source_ip": "34.72.12.9",
  "trace_id": "trace-444"
}

Appendix B — Contact list:
- Security lead: Leah Martinez (leah@redwood.ai)
- SRE on-call: Tom Benoit (pager: oncall-sre)
- SOC: Priya Singh (soc@redwood.ai)

End of worksheet.
